title: Germany – Canteen management services – BV1 26 MoKa RK N/008 - Bewirtschaftete Betreuung am StO Bremen (Modell Kasino)
description: Der Auftragnehmer (AN) verpflichtet sich, die bewirtschaftete Betreuung des Kasinos in der Scharnhorst-Kaserne, Niedersachsendamm 67/69 in 28201 Bremen (Liegenschaft), wie im Einzelnen in der Leistungsbeschreibung in Anhang 1 zum Dienstleistungsvertrag festgelegt, auszuführen und durch eigenverantwortliche betriebswirtschaftliche Planung einschließlich eigenem Waren- und Personaleinsatz sicherzustellen. Für die Erbringung der geforderten Dienstleistung erhält der AN eine monatliche Vergütung, deren Höhe und Kalkulation vom AN in seinem Angebot anzugeben ist. Die durch den AN im Rahmen des Kasinobetriebs erwirtschafteten Einnahmen verbleiben ebenfalls bei ihm; erst wenn der von ihm innerhalb eines Kalenderjahres erzielte Umsatz zuzüglich der vom Auftraggeber (AG) gezahlten Vergütung die für den Kasinobetrieb entstehenden Kosten übersteigt, reduziert sich die Vergütung durch den AG um einen Teil des die Kosten übersteigenden Betrages. Die Vertragslaufzeit beträgt fünf Jahre (mit zweimaliger Verlängerungsmöglichkeit um jeweils 1 Jahr). Als Leistungsbeginn ist aktuell der 1. Juli 2027 vorgesehen; letzterer wird ausdrücklich nicht zugesichert, sondern kann sich im Verlauf des Vergabeverfahrens verschieben. Leistungsgegenstand ist die Bereitstellung eines attraktiven gastronomischen Angebots durch den AN, bei dem neben kundenorientierten Speisen eine Atmosphäre geschaffen wird, die zum Verweilen einlädt und ein geselliges Miteinander ermöglicht. Der AN hat bestimmte Gerichte und Getränke zu vertraglich festgelegten Preisen anzubieten (siehe Anhang 9 zum Dienstleistungsvertrag, Basissortiment). Die Preise werden jährlich im Februar an die Preisentwicklung angepasst. Die Verfügbarkeit des Basissortiments ist sicherzustellen. Bei allen über die Gerichte des Basissortiments hinausgehenden Gerichten ist der AN in der Preisgestaltung frei. Für den Betrieb des Kasinos werden dem AN vom Auftraggeber (AG) Räumlichkeiten (einschließl. Außenanlage) und darin befindliches Liegenschaftsmaterial zur Verfügung gestellt. Die Überlassung erfolgt unentgeltlich, d. h. es wird kein Mietzins erhoben. Auch die Kosten für die durch den AG erbrachten Liegenschaftsbetriebsleistungen (Facility Management wie z. B. Medienversorgung (Wasser, Strom, Wärme), Abwasserentsorgung sowie Abfallentsorgung) übernimmt der AG. Einzelheiten sind in den Regelungen zur Überlassung von Liegenschaften der Bundeswehr an Dritte als Auftragnehmer [RÜL] (Anhang 3 zum Dienstleistungsvertrag) geregelt. Die Ausstattung der Gasträume des Kasinos erfolgt teilweise durch den AN auf dessen Kosten. Auch ist der AN verantwortlich für die Anschaffung von Gläsern, Geschirr und Besteck sowie des Kassensystems. Einzelheiten sind den Vertragsdokumenten, insbesondere dem Dienstleistungsvertrag und der Leistungsbeschreibung in Anhang 1 zum Dienstleistungsvertrag, zu entnehmen. In dem hier betroffenen Ausschreibungsverfahren BV1 26 MoKa RKN/008 enthalten die Dokumente "Leistungsbeschreibung" und "Dienstleistungsvertrag" als Verschlusssachen eingestufte Bestandteile und werden daher nicht im Teilnahmewettbewerb veröffentlicht. Diese Dokumente werden erst in der Angebotsphase bekanntgegeben. Teilnahmeantrag: Es ist ein formloser Teilnahmeantrag in deutscher Sprache auf dem offiziellen Briefbogen Ihres Unternehmens über die eVergabe-Plattform einzureichen, der entweder mit fortgeschrittener Signatur, qualifizierter Signatur oder Firmenstempel/Unterschrift eingescannt zu versehen ist. Der Teilnahmeantrag hat eine Selbstdarstellung des Unternehmens zu enthalten, die etwa 1/2 bis 1 Seite DIN A4 lang sein soll. In der Selbstdarstellung muss die Erfüllung der Eignungskriterien bestätigt werden. Folgende Unterlagen müssen dem Teilnahmeantrag ausgefüllt beigefügt werden: (1) Formular BAAINBW B-V31 Erklärung Verschlusssachen; (2) Formular B-V034 Eigenerklärung Ausschlussgründe; (3) Formular Erklärung RUS Sanktionen; (4) Formular BAAINBW-B096a Merkblatt Verschlusssachen; (5) Versicherungsnachweis (oder ausgefüllte Eigenerklärung Versicherungsschutz). Ggfls. Erklärung zum Schutz von Verschlusssachen für Unterauftragnehmer (B-V032) Ggfls. Erklärung Bietergemeinschaft (B-V047) Die Formulare 1 bis 4 müssen entweder mit fortgeschrittener Signatur, qualifizierter Signatur oder Firmenstempel/Unterschrift eingescannt versehen sein. Bei Vorliegen einer Bietergemeinschaft ist zusätzlich das Formular B-V047 Bietergemeinschaft beizufügen. Da die als Verschlusssachen eingestuften Unterlagen per E-Mail (verschlüsselt) übersandt werden, ist im Teilnahmeantrag eine sichere E-Mail-Adresse zu benennen, unter der die vertrauliche Bearbeitung der Unterlagen sichergestellt ist. Nach Abschluss des Teilnahmewettbewerbs erhalten die zugelassenen Unternehmen eine Angebotsaufforderung. Das daraufhin einzureichende Angebot hat verbindlich zu sein. Der Auftraggeber behält sich den Zuschlag auf die Erstangebote ebenso vor, wie Verhandlungen durchzuführen. Es wird darauf hingewiesen, dass es dem Auftragnehmer untersagt ist, Personal, welches die Liegenschaft betreten muss, mit einer Staatsangehörigkeit zu Ländern im Sinne des § 13 Abs. 1 S.1 Nr. 17 des Sicherheitsüberprüfungsgesetzes (SÜG) (siehe sog. Staatenliste) einzusetzen. Personen dieser Länder erhalten keinen Zutritt zum militärischen Sicherheitsbereich.

title: Shropshire 0-25 Public Health Nursing Service (PHNS)
description: The Authority is seeking a provider to deliver an integrated 0-19 (up to 25 where appropriate) Healthy Child Programme, encompassing Health Visiting, School Nursing and Family Nurse Partnership services across Shropshire. The service will support children, young people and families through a community-based, preventative model that promotes positive health and wellbeing outcomes, reduces inequalities and responds to local need through population health management and local intelligence. The Provider will be expected to work collaboratively with health, social care, education and wider stakeholders to deliver joined-up, neighbourhood-based services. Delivery will be supported by a multidisciplinary workforce comprising qualified clinical and non-clinical staff, with Qualified Public Health Nurses providing professional leadership, clinical oversight and safeguarding expertise. This procurement is being undertaken in accordance with the Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023 using the Competitive Process

title: Romania – Hardware installation services – ENSOC Hosting Site PT ICT Infrastructure (Computing, Storage, Networking, Cybersecurity)
description: The ENSOC Cross-border Cyber Hub Platform (hereinafter ENSOC CBP) envisages the construction of a European Cybersecurity Alert System (ECAS) as foreseen by the EU’s Cybersecurity Strategy. It aims to strengthen capacities to analyse, detect and prevent cyber threats and provide support to the production of high-quality intelligence on cyber threats, notably through the exchange of data from various sources, public and private as well as through the sharing of the state-of-the-art tools and jointly developing cyber detection, analysis and prevention capabilities in a trusted environment. The ENSOC consortium is a collective effort of a group of Member States (LU, PT, ES, AT, NL, RO and IT), which targets improving the security of EU stakeholders and support both CSIRTs and SOCs by providing a common space of cyber intelligence sharing, incident coordination, automation, and situation awareness in order to improve defensive capabilities. This procurement procedure concerns the infrastructure hardware and related software (including a backup solution), and the related services that will be necessary to serve as a backbone for the activities of the ENSOC Consortium's Member - Portugal. The infrastructure will be hosted and operated in Lisbon in the Centro Nacional de Cibersegurança (CNCS) Headquarters.

title: Request for Expression of Interest (RFEOI) for New CADSS/MAJAID Facility
description: DEFENCE CONSTRUCTION CANADA (DCC) – TRS18081_73944 – New CADSS/MAJAID Facility, Trenton, Ontario Defence Construction Canada (DCC) invites general contractors to express their interest in providing all labour, materials, and equipment necessary to build a new warehouse and operations facility to support the Combat Aerial Delivery Support Section/Major Air Disaster (CADSS/MAJAID) Unit. This Request for Expression of Interest (RFEOI) is the first step of a two-step solicitation process, the second step being the Tender Phase.  Only general contractors that have expressed their interest through the Electronic Bidding System prior to the closing date and time of this RFEOI will be invited to submit a proposal at the second stage. Only submissions received in accordance with the requirements of the Electronic Bidding System will be considered. Only the general contractors who will have responded to this RFEOI will be invited to submit a bid during the Tender Phase. DCC reserves the right to terminate this solicitation at the end of the RFEOI. As part of Canada’s commitment to maximize the participation of Indigenous Businesses, bidders are advised that this solicitation includes an Indigenous Benefits Plan (IBP). The Contractor will have to include Indigenous businesses (or eligible joint ventures) as subcontractors or suppliers to this project. Further details will be provided in the Tender phase. This solicitation is being conducted in accordance with the requirements set out in the Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA), the Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) and the World Trade Organization Agreement on Government Procurement (WTO-GPA). 1. Project background The CADSS/MAJAID Facility project at 8 Wing CFB Trenton consists of the construction of a new 1,554 m² warehouse and operations facility to support the Combat Aerial Delivery Support Section/Major Air Disaster (CADSS/MAJAID) Unit. The work comprises general contracting services and the supply and installation of all labour and materials required to construct the facility, including associated building systems and site infrastructure. The facility will provide space for parachute inspection, drying, preparation, and packing activities, while also accommodating administrative functions, operational storage requirements, and material handling activities. The proposed facility includes a dedicated carpentry shop, warehouse storage areas, administrative office space, and specialized infrastructure to support operational equipment and warehouse activities involving forklifts and other machinery. Key features include storage and racking systems, a 20-tonne overhead bridge crane, and a parachute drying tower. The facility includes a steel-framed structure enclosed with prefinished metal cladding and high-performance insulated wall assemblies. The roofing system consists of a steel deck structure with a two-ply modified bitumen membrane and insulated roof assembly. Mechanical systems include plumbing, sanitary and storm drainage, natural gas distribution, compressed air, HVAC, make-up air units, ventilation systems, heat recovery, dust collection, and building controls. Fire protection and life-safety systems include a wet-pipe sprinkler system, fire alarm system, fire department connection, emergency lighting, exit signage, and associated monitoring and control equipment. Site works include new water, sanitary, storm, electrical, communications, and site power services, including a new 300 kVA pad-mounted transformer, underground electrical distribution, communications duct banks, parking receptacles, and utility connections to support facility operations. Exterior site development also includes landscaping and paving requirements, including paved areas to support vehicle access, parking, loading, and facility operations, together with associated site restoration and landscaping. The project will meet all applicable codes and standards. 2. Documents Technical plans and specifications are not available during this RFEOI and will be provided during the Tender Phase; however, the Standard Construction Contract Documents for Electronic Bidding, DCL 250E, are available on DCC's website: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/forms. Tenderers are advised that this contract is subject to DCC's Procurement Code of Conduct, which can be downloaded at https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/forms. A contractor or supplier who has been declared ineligible or suspended by Public Services and Procurement Canada under its Ineligibility and Suspension Policy and whose period of ineligibility or suspension may not have expired will not be able to proceed to the second stage. Bid security will be required during the Tender Phase in accordance with DCL193E- Instructions for Bidders for Electronic Bidding item 5. 3.Estimate The Rough Order Magnitude estimate for this Contract is $12.5 Million (Current Year $). This amount includes all construction costs, on-site work (including all required services, parking, and landscaping), site utilities, necessary redundant mechanical systems, communication conduits and wiring, backup power equipment, built-in equipment, built-in furniture, and inflation to achieve substantial completion. This amount excludes HST, design costs, travel and disbursements, consultant fees and expenses, movable equipment and furniture, IT equipment and contingencies. 4. title: ET025-270778.B - Pangnirtung Harbour Improvements - RFP
description: Please note that late submissions will not be considered or accepted. Public Works & Government Services Canada (PWGSC) requires the services of a Civil Engineering firm with expertise in the design and construction of marine infrastructure in the Arctic environment and small craft harbours, acting as the prime consultant with a multi-disciplinary team of sub-consultants for the delivery of services required for this project. Fisheries and Oceans Canada, Small Craft Harbours (DFO-SCH) requires proposals from Engineering Consultants for professional services to carry out the scope of work outlined under Section 2.0 Required Services for improvements to the Small Craft Harbour (SCH) at Pangnirtung, NU. The harbour supports inshore and offshore commercial fisheries, ensuring that local fishing operations have access to safe harbours and landing facilities. Improvements to the DFO-SCH harbour in Pangnirtung are required to support safe access to the land and sea in the context of rapid environmental changes in the Arctic and in support of community fish harvesting and marine mammal harvest. Harbour improvements are required at this time including replacement of floating wharves, improvements to the harbour’s launch ramp, and maintenance dredging of the entrance channel and mooring basin. See the Terms of Reference for more details.

description: Les principales prestations de l'accord-cadre à bons de commande sont décrites ci-après : Pour des projets de construction d’installations nucléaires ou de travaux de modifications d’installations individuelles et d’ICPE (Installation Classée pour la Protection de l'Environnement) en exploitation ou en démantèlement : • réalisation d’études, d’analyses, de bilans, de documents de synthèse et de dossiers réglementaires de sûreté nucléaires, et contribution à leur instruction par les autorités concernées ; • définition et gestion de la remontée de conformité au travers des exigences de sûreté ; • gestion de la configuration sûreté des installations en lien avec l’ingénierie système (outils/processus spécifiques, gestion du référentiel et des outils de gestion d’événements) ; • élaboration et mise en œuvre d’outils et de processus d’ingénierie de sûreté transverses ; • management et animation des équipes. L’exécution des prestations pourra se faire sur les différents sites de la DAM ainsi que sur la base navale de Toulon. Le marché comporte : • une phase de réversibilité entrante de 6 mois (optionnelle) ; • une phase de « production » composée de 36 mois fermes et 36 mois optionnels ; • une phase de réversibilité sortante concomitante sur les 6 derniers mois de la phase « production » en cours (optionnelle).

title: Protected Anti-Jam Tactical SATCOM (PATS) Operations Center (PATSOC) Mission Operations Services Request for Information (RFI)
description: Section I: PTES Description & Background Protected Anti-Jam Tactical SATCOM (PATS) provides worldwide, beyond line of sight (BLOS), Anti-Jam, Low Probability of Intercept (LPI) communications to tactical warfighters in both benign and contested environments. PATS uses the Protected Tactical Waveform (PTW) to enable forward-deployed users and coalition/international partners to fill capability gaps for protected communications. PATS employs a military web-based planning and operations architecture and communications hubs to enable existing or new terminals with a PTW-capable modem. The PTW can be used on any PTW processed or non-processed wideband satellite communications platform, providing mission critical communications with varying levels of protection depending on the SATCOM environment, satellite system, and available resources. PTW supports high throughput in benign conditions and adapts automatically to reduced capacity in favor of increased robustness for contested environments such as jamming, terminal movement, and weather degradation. PTW also provides logical and cryptographic separation of user groups to maintain operational security. PATS will be implemented in phases aligned with Protected Tactical Enterprise Service (PTES) ground capabilities. PTES is the enabling ground component of PATS, providing operational planning, mission and network management, and hubs for PTW networks using Wideband Global SATCOM (WGS) and commercial transponded SATCOM systems. WGS PATS Phase capability provides PTW over WGS, and Commercial Satellite Communications (COMSATCOM) Phase increases flexibility and resiliency by supporting PTW over COMSATCOM. Protected Tactical Satellite (PTS) Phase adds PTW over PTS satellites for near-peer jamming protection. Section II: RFI Objective The purpose of this RFI is to understand industry capabilities, risks, staffing approaches, recommended contract structure, transition considerations, and relevant experience associated with delivering mission planning and mission operations described in this request. This Request for Information (RFI) is issued to identify and gather information from sources capable of providing full-spectrum staffing for the Protected Anti-Jam Tactical SATCOM (PATS) Operations Center (PATSOC). The Government seeks information regarding industry capability to establish, staff, train, manage, and sustain a cleared operational workforce supporting planning, provisioning, monitoring, management, cybersecurity coordination, operational reporting, and execution of PTW networks. Government anticipates utilizing contractor personnel to fulfill designated onsite operator positions for each phase of performance, as discussed in Section III, Table 1, below. The anticipated NAICS for this acquisition is 517810 and the size standard is $40,000,000.00. Small businesses and Government entities with existing contract vehicles are encouraged to respond to this request. Section III: RFI Scope The contractor shall be responsible for management oversight and for providing qualified and cleared personnel. The contractor shall conduct proficiency and recurring training, maintaining situational awareness of COI processes and procedures regarding mission planning and mission operations, updating training, technical manuals, TTPs, continuity planning, and any relevant material required to perform mission planning and mission operations accordingly. The contractor shall staff the PATSOC and conduct mission planning and mission operations using Government-provided MMS, NMS, KMS, PATS PVT, and associated applications, while interfacing with additional tools required to perform and support mission planning and mission operations. PATSOC personnel are expected to manage account administration, registrar functions, role-based access control enabling mission planning and mission operations. These functions will extend to the COI enabling the concept of operations. The contractor may support phases of the operational lifecycle, including pre-operational test preparation, IT&E/MOT&E support, discrepancy report and problem report resolution, regression testing, transition to CFC Trial Period operations, sustained operational execution, situational awareness reporting, Continuity of Operations preparation and execution, and transition to a future operations and maintenance construct. The Government anticipates that the phases of support described herein may be revised, restructured, or further subdivided based on industry responses to this RFI. Phase 1 PATSOC Pre-Mission Operations Establish PATSOC mission operations after PATSOC Site Acceptance and prior to the start of Integrated Test & Evaluation (IT&E). Provide M-F 8hr staffing to include but not limited to: planning and operations manager, mission planner, network controller, help desk, system and network administrator, registrar, cryptographic operator, database administrator, and training manager. Pre-Mission Operations positions may be reduced by the Government to a subset of position roles defined in the PTES System Concept and listed above. Pre-Mission Operations shall conduct initial preparation and support execution of IT&E, Multi-service Operational Test & Evaluation (MOT&E) and all other events related to test and evaluation of the PTES system. Pre-Mission Operations shall prepare for mission objectives defined in the PATS Concept of Operations (CONOPS), and the PTES Capability Development Document (CDD). The following summary is provided to clarify the focus of the anticipated Pre-Operations Mission Support phase. It is intended to help industry understand the type and scope of staffing the Government may require prior to the start of the IT&E evaluation of the PTES system. Beginning after PATSOC Site Acceptance and approximately 90 days prior to the IT&E dry-run event and continuing until the start of the CFC Trial Period. Provide sufficient staffing to support Monday � Friday 8 hours a day for IT&E and MOT&E test events, including dry runs, test community coordination, workspace familiarization, access readiness, and operational readiness preparation. Develop and submit a PATSOC Staffing Plan identifying proposed roles, responsibilities, and staffing quantities for the Pre-Operations Mission Support period. Operate, evaluate, and use the Mission Management System (MMS), PATS Planning Verification Tool (PVT), Network Management System (NMS), Key Management System (KMS) and associated applications for network/mission planning, product generation, monitoring, management, trouble ticket response, network management, account management, registrar functions, and COI situational awareness. Develop, maintain, and provide updates to the PATSOC training program, update technical manuals, develop and update Tactics, Techniques, and Procedures (TTPs), maintain shift logs, create and update shift changeover briefings, create and customize dashboards, and prepare trending data for official reports and for the COI. Perform registrar functions and PTES account management. Identify and document discrepancies, perform root cause analysis, support Discrepancy Review Board (DRB) prioritization and resolution, conduct regression testing, and support Government disposition planning. Support Government preparation and execution of transition to the CFC Trial Period and sustained operations. Phase 2 Interim Contract Support (ICS) PATSOC Mission Operations Provide sustained PATSOC mission operations staff starting two weeks prior to start of Combat Forces Command (CFC) Trial Period and continuing through Full Operational Capability (FOC) declaration or until terminated by the Government. Provide 24/7 operations floor staff to include but not limited to: planning and operations manager, mission planner, network controller, help desk, system and network administrator and registrar. title: J066--GRECC Preventive Maintenance Contract, Durham VAMC
description: Solicitation Number: 36C24627Q0092 0002 Notice Type: Amendment to Solicitation The Department of Veterans Network Contracting Office (NCO 06), Hampton, VA on behalf of the Durham VA Health Care System (VAHCS), intends to solicit a Small Business set-aside for Preventative Maintenance services for centrifuges and other included instruments for the Durham VA Medical Center Geriatric Research, Education, and Clinical Center (GRECC) located at 508 Fulton Street, Durham, NC 27705-3875. This pre-solicitation announcement publicizes the Department of Veterans Affairs intent to solicit for preventative maintenance services for centrifuges and other included equipment. A Firm-Fixed price contract is anticipated to be awarded. The VA anticipates issuing a Small Business set-aside solicitation for this requirement. The solicitation and any amendments will be available on System for Awards Management (SAM)website in Contract Opportunities at http://www.SAM.gov. Potential quoters will be responsible for downloading copies of the solicitation (and any subsequent amendments) from that website, and no hard copies will be made available. The solicitation will provide instructions to offerors about the quote submission process. Prospective Quoters are encouraged to register their interest in the solicitation on the SAM.gov website so that they are notified of the issuance of the solicitation and any amendments. Quotes will be evaluated for award after the solicitation has closed. In accordance with FAR 52.204-7, System for Award Management, prospective quoters must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) database under the applicable NAICS Code. Firms may obtain SAM information at https://www.sam.gov. To be eligible for award, contractors must be registered in SAM. Registration is free and potential quoters are encouraged to visit the SAM website and register as soon as possible. Questions concerning this announcement should be directed to the Contract Specialist using the e-mail link provided. No hard copies of the solicitation will be provided. Telephone requests for information or questions will NOT be accepted. Please email questions to Monique Cordero at Monique.Cordero@va.gov and ensure that the subject line includes Solicitation No. 36C24627Q0092 and reference your Company Name. Contracting Office Address: Department of Veterans Affairs Network Contracting Office (NCO6) Bldg. 27 Averill Drive, Hampton, VA 23667

title: France – Consultative engineering and construction services – Mission d'assistance à maîtrise d'ouvrage globale du projet ValEDOM : structuration institutionnelle, passation d'une concession et mise en service d'une Unité de Valorisation Energétique
description: Les prestations consistent en une mission d'Assistance à maîtrise d'ouvrage (AMO) globale nécessaire à la préfiguration, la structuration institutionnelle, la passation d'une concession et la réalisation du projet d'une unité de valorisation énergétique (UVE) de dimension interdépartementale dénommé ValEDOM (Valorisation Energétique des Déchets de l'Orne et de la Manche), d'une capacité de traitement comprise entre 130Kt/an et 160Kt/an. L'énergie produite alimentera le réseau de chaleur de Saint-Lô (en cours de réalisation) et l'électricité produite sera injectée sur le réseau national. Ce projet fera l'objet d'une concession en vue de la réalisation de travaux et de l'exploitation du site, sous réserve de validation des membres du futur GAC. Il est précisé que le titulaire du marché (candidat unique ou tous les membres en cas de groupement) ne pourra pas à répondre à la consultation pour la procédure passation de la concession de l'opération

title: MilLife Learning Management System Support Service
description: The government requires a contractor to provide support services for its learning management system, which consists of the MilLife Learning platform, maintained under a separate contract, and online learning environment https://millifelearning.militaryonesource.mil. The contractor shall support a portfolio of approximately 90�120 online courses, microlearning products, and related learning assets, including new development, updates, maintenance, third-party course support, reporting, accessibility review, and operational support as directed by the Government. The learning environment shall apply, at a minimum, evidence-based adult learning practices, including adult learning theory, Bloom�s Taxonomy, Kirkpatrick�s levels of evaluation, Merrill�s principles of instruction, multimedia learning principles, and Human-Centered Design. The system includes the MilLife Learning platform, Student Information System, User Information System, Blackboard platform, and related tools that support course delivery, learner access, content management, reporting, analytics, communications, and operations. The contractor shall identify, develop, test, and implement AI-enabled tools, workflows, and technologies, as approved by the Government, to streamline operations, reduce duplication, improve productivity, achieve measurable cost savings and cost avoidance while ensuring all products remain accurate, current, accessible, secure, and compliant with applicable requirements.

title: France – Computer-related services – Mise à disposition en mode SAAS d’une solution numérique de veille et de détection d’éventuels détournements d’usage des données du système d'information de l'ANTENJ et prestations associées ("DADRIM")
description: L’Agence nationale des techniques d'enquêtes numériques judiciaires (ANTENJ) pilote les outils régaliens mis en oeuvre en matière d’interceptions de communications électroniques et autres techniques numériques d’enquête. À ce titre, elle met à disposition des magistrats et enquêteurs plusieurs outils informatiques composant le Système d’information des techniques d’enquêtes numériques judiciaires (SITENJ). Dans ce cadre, la présente procédure a pour objet la mise à disposition, par un éditeur de solution standard du marché, d'une solution permettant de surveiller activement l’utilisation illicite éventuelle dans l’espace numérique de données issues du SITENJ qui, en grande majorité, sont strictement soumises au secret de l’enquête ou de l’instruction. Le détail des prestations et fonctionnalités figure dans le dossier de consultation mais la solution doit a minima offrir un service de : 1) veille permanente et de remontée d’information à destination des utilisateurs de l’administration (détection automatisée et alerte) ; 2) recherche active sur demande desdits utilisateurs (détection sur la base des éléments transmis).

title: France – Construction work for bridges and tunnels, shafts and subways – LOT 1 Travaux de terrassement, de fabrication et pose d’éléments de 3 lignes de galeries secondaires du RSGE
description: Avant de réaliser les travaux de construction des ouvrages de stockage de déchets radioactifs sur le Centre de stockage de l’Aube (CSA), il convient de procéder à la mise en place des galeries sous ouvrages. Ces galeries souterraines (éléments préfabriqués) ont notamment pour fonction principale de permettre l’accès sous les ouvrages pendant les phases d’exploitation et de surveillance du site (d’une durée minimale de 300 ans) afin de faire des contrôles des éventuels écoulements issus des ouvrages de stockage qui sont récupérés dans un réseau spécifique appelé « Réseau Séparatif Gravitaire Enterré » (RSGE) implanté dans ces galeries. Ces galeries sont réalisées sous les interlignes des lignes d’ouvrages, une galerie desservant 2 lignes d’ouvrages contigus. Les travaux objet du présent avis de marché comprennent principalement : • Les travaux de terrassement de grande masse pour un volume estimatif de 20000m3, • Les travaux de terrassement pour un volume estimatif de 75000m3 de sable notamment pour la mise en place des 3 galeries enterrées, • La démolition de longrines dans l’emprise de la zone de creusement, • La fourniture et la pose de 3 lignes de galeries préfabriquées sur approximativement 265ml et des canalisations intérieures. La dimension intérieure de chaque élément de galerie est d’environ 2m50 en hauteur et 1m30 en largeur. • La reconstruction des tronçons de jonction avec la galerie principale, • La fourniture des longueurs droites des canalisations du RSGE et des piézomètres, • Le rabattement de la nappe pendant les travaux, • La substitution des sols en place par un remblai en sable avec les matériaux du site • Le remblaiement des excavations exécutées pour la pose des galeries jusqu’aux cotes prescrites sur les plans guides de remblai, • La fourniture et la mise en œuvre d’un béton de rattrapage sur le toit des galeries pour établir le plan horizontal de fondation des longrines inter-ouvrages, • La note de calculs d’exécution des éléments de galerie principale (coulés en place, ou préfabriqués partiellement), • La note de calculs d’exécution des différents éléments et clavages de galerie inter-ouvrages, • La note de calcul du dispositif de rabattement de nappe, montrant en particulier la conformité avec les exigences liées au bac de décantation, • Les plans d’exécutions des terrassements et des remblaiements, figurant notamment les réseaux permettant la maîtrise des eaux pluviales après le chantier, • Les plans de coffrage et de ferraillage des éléments de galerie inter-ouvrages, • Les plans de coffrage et de ferraillage des tronçons de galerie principale à reconstituer, • Les plans de coffrage et de ferraillage des clavages, • Les plans d’implantation des pointes filtrantes, • Les plans d’exécutions des ouvrages de serrurerie : trappe de fermeture, échelle de sortie en extrémité des galeries inter-ouvrages et marche pour accès dans la galerie principale. L’Andra étant certifiée ISO 9001, ISO 14001 et ISO 45001, le titulaire mettra en place, pour l’exécution de ses missions, une organisation de modèle « ISO 9001, version 2015, notamment en matière : - De gestion des compétences, - De gestion de la documentation, - De traitement des non-conformités. Au titre des dispositions prises pour le contrôle de ses travaux, le titulaire est tenu de : - De formaliser et programmer les actions de contrôle appropriées, - De faire effectuer ces contrôles par du personnel qualifié, - De prouver que les contrôles sont effectués, - De démontrer que les prestations sont conformes aux spécifications. Pour les prestations réalisées sur le CSA, le titulaire prend en compte les exigences de l’arrêté du 7 février 2012. Cet arrêté fixe les règles générales relatives aux installations nucléaires de base. Le titulaire devra la totalité des procédures d’exécution et de contrôle du Plan Qualité nécessaires à l’exécution des travaux. Les procédures à établir sont au minimum : - Procédure d’entreposage et de gestion des produits dangereux et inflammables, - Procédure d’élimination des déchets produits sur le chantier avec les dispositions préparatoires suivantes : - La liste des centres de stockage et de regroupement ou des unités de recyclage ou des lieux de réutilisation où seront acheminés les différents déchets à évacuer, - Les méthodes qui seront employées pour ne pas mélanger les différents déchets, - Procédures en usine comprenant : - Procédure de mise en place des éléments de galerie sur parc de stockage en usine et/ou sur chantier, - Procédure de finitions et réparations en cas de petits défauts en usine et sur site, - Procédure de démolitions, d’excavations et remblaiement : - Procédure d’exécution des rabattements de nappe comprenant le suivi des débits et la mesure des quantités de sable décanté, - Procédure d’exécutions des excavations, - Procédure de démolition des longrines et amorces de longrines et des regards en tête de ligne, - Procédure d’exécution des dépôts de matériaux sur le Centre de l’Aube, - Procédure d’exécution du remblaiement des fouilles, - Procédure de réalisation des enrobés, - Procédure de réalisation des galeries : - Procédure d’exécution des galeries coulées en place ou partiellement préfabriquées, - Procédure d’exécution des clavages de galerie principale, - Procédure de pose de galerie inter-ouvrages, - Procédure de réparation en cas de défaut d’étanchéité, - Procédure de réalisation du béton de rattrapage sur les galeries, - Procédure de pose du complexe d’argile gonflante (orégonite) au droit des joints. - Procédure des contrôles à réaliser sur les éléments de galeries (en usine, à réception sur chantier, durant la phase de mise en œuvre et à la reconstitution des sols pour les opérations de terrassement, - Procédure de stockage des éprouvettes destinées aux essais du béton de rattrapage, - … Les étapes de la procédure et les modalités de sélection des candidats sont décrites au chapitre 2 du Règlement de consultation de procédure avec negociation.

title: 27M-082A-PR
description: This is a request for information (RFI) / SOURCES SOUGHT SYNOPSIS. This request is not a solicitation (Request for Proposal or Request for Quotations) or a promise to issue a solicitation in the future. Responses to this notice are not considered offers and cannot be accepted by the government to form a binding contract. The purpose of this request for information is in support of market research being conducted by the Air Force Metrology Calibration Program (AFMETCAL) to identify potential sources and gather information on current capabilities within the market. This synopsis is for planning purposes only and is NOT to be construed as a commitment by the Government nor will the Government pay for information solicited hereunder. All costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the responding party's expense. The level of security clearance and amount of foreign participation in this requirement has not been determined. All information received in response to this RFI that is marked PROPRIETARY will be handled accordingly. Proprietary information will be safeguarded in accordance with the applicable Government regulations. Proprietary information or trade secrets should be clearly identified. If, after reviewing these documents, you desire to participate in the market research, you should provide documentation that supports your company's capability in meeting these requirements. Failure to provide documentation may result in the government being unable to adequately assess your capabilities. If you lack sufficient experience in a particular area, please provide details explaining how you would overcome the lack of experience/capabilities in order to perform that portion of the requirement (i.e., teaming, subcontracting, etc.) Both large and small businesses are encouraged to participate in this Market Research. Joint ventures or teaming arrangements are encouraged. Currently there are no funds available for this acquisition. AFMETCAL is seeking sources to procure and deliver Tire Inflator Calibrators. The Tire Inflator Calibrator (TIC) is a rugged diagnostic system used to test, verify, and calibrate the accuracy of hand-held pneumatic tire inflator kits. These inflator kits are critical for maintaining correct tire pressures across the aircraft fleet, and the calibrator ensures their built-in pressure gauges and relief valves read and perform correctly. The Air Force Metrology and Calibration Program (AFMETCAL) is seeking to procure up to 76 units of this system to support calibration operations. The system consists of two primary operational areas: a Supply Section and a Measurement Section. The Supply Section connects directly to a workshop air source and uses a pressure gauge, a safety relief valve, and a fine-tuning metering valve to deliver a precise, controlled stream of air into the tire inflator assembly being tested. The Measurement Section then receives the air released from the tire inflator assembly. It routes this air through an isolation valve into a specialized chamber (which acts as a mock "tire" to simulate realistic air expansion) and measures it using highly accurate digital pressure gauges. Interested vendors should submit a brief capability statement including company information (DUNS, CAGE, business size), relevant experience, and rough order of magnitude pricing. The NAICS code assigned to this acquisition is 334515 with a size standard of 750 employees. The total estimated quantity is 76 units over 6 years. Reconditioned, remanufactured, or used material is not acceptable for this item. Offerors responding to this sources sought market research notice must: (1) state whether you are a small or large business, if you are the manufacturer or provide the name of the manufacturer and size info of product you would be offering and the socioeconomic status and indicate small disadvantaged or woman-owned business, veteran owned, service disabled veteran owned, 8(a) historically black college or university or minority institution (HBCU/MI), or a historically underutilized business zone (HUBZone) (2) provide sales history including recent sales to commercial companies (3) advise if your product is a commercial item or if it will be modified; if not commercial at this time, will you be offering this item to the general public in the future. (4) advise if you have the item on a GSA schedule or other Government contract include front page of schedule and the page showing the part is on award (5) provide information concerning the technical capabilities of the product you are interested in offering, including commercial literature/brochures and warranty. Describe any awards you have been involved in that are the same as or similar to what is described in this RFI. Include any other pertinent information which would enable the government to assess your firm�s capabilities (6) advise if you accept the Government purchase card (7) Provide Point of Contact including: company/ institute name, address, phone number and email address (8) provide assigned Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) Code (9) Verify if your company/institute is listed in the System for Award Management (SAM) (10) State if your company is domestically or foreign owned (if foreign owned, please indicate the country of ownership) (11) Advise how much time you would need to submit a technical proposal if a solicitation is issued (12) provide an estimated price for one each, an estimated price for the total quantity and provide any price quantity discounts based on the total estimated quantity (13) include estimated delivery time for shipment. description: Portfolio Acquisition Executive Maritime (PAEM) is issuing solicitation N00024-26-R-4439 to procure a series of Multiple Ship Sustainment Partnership (MSSP) Single Award Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (SA-IDIQ) Contracts to complete Fleet Maintenance Availabilities and Incremental Selected Restricted Availabilities (ISRAs) on DDG-51 Class ships homeported in Norfolk, VA. Fixed Price with Award Fees (FPAF) Contracts will be awarded across Facilitized and Non-Facilitized Lots. Facilitized Lot includes Fleet Maintenance Availabilities and CNO scheduled ISRAs, to be completed on specific DDG-51 class ships that are scheduled to complete ISRAs over the MSSP period of performance. The scope of this lot includes all efforts necessary to support continuous coordination, planning and preparation between contractor and government to complete Fleet Maintenance Availabilities and ISRAs including, but not limited to, inter-availability preparation and administration (IAPA) support, inspections and assessments, engineering and design support, specification and other government furnished information reviews, and material procurement and logistics support. Unless otherwise specified in a Delivery Order Solicitation, all delivery orders for Fleet Maintenance Availabilities will be performed at the Government facility and all ISRAs will be performed in-plant at a Contactor-provided facility. The Navy will solicit this Lot on a full and open basis. The Navy intends to award up to three (3) Facilitized Lot contracts. The number will be determined at contract award based on the number of acceptable proposals received. Non-Facilitized Lot includes Fleet Maintenance Availabilities only, to be completed on specific DDG-51 class ships that are not scheduled to complete ISRAs over the MSSP period of performance. The scope of this lot includes all efforts necessary to support continuous coordination, planning and preparation between contractor and government to complete Fleet Maintenance Availabilities including, but not limited to, IAPA support, inspections and assessments, engineering and design support, specification and other government furnished information reviews, and material procurement and logistics support. Unless otherwise specified in a Delivery Order Solicitation, all Delivery Orders will be performed at the Governments facility. The Navy will solicit this Lot as a Small Business Set Aside. The Navy intends to award up to three (3) Non-Facilitized Lot contracts. The number will be determined at contract award based on the number of acceptable proposals received. Each contract will include three (3) one-year ordering periods. The supply being procured is the repaired, mission-ready vessel, which is returned to service within the Fleet. title: Design/Build Maintenance and Repair Army Reserve (MRAR), Area Maintenance Support Activity (AMSA) 21, JBMDL, NJ
description: 10/08/2026: ***Anticipated Solicitation Date, Solicitation Number as well as building description have been updated*** 08/30/2026: ***Anticipated Solicitation Date as well as building description has been updated*** ***THE SOLICITATION NUMBER HAS BEEN UPDATED TO W912QR27RA004*** DESCRIPTION: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Louisville District intends to issue a Request for Proposal (RFP) W912QR27RA004 for the Maintenance and Repair Army Reserve (MRAR) of Area Maintenance Support Activity (AMSA) 21 at Joint Base McGuire-Dix-Lakehurst (JBMDL) in Burlington, New Jersey. The project will repair failing facility components and extend the economic life of the facility by 25 years, providing a modern maintenance facility that enables readiness for the Army Reserve units located in the surrounding area. The project scope includes the repair of the failing HVAC and electrical systems, the removal of non-structural interior walls to right-size rooms and create open flexible workspaces as required, the repair/replacement/upgrade of light fixtures with code compliant units, the installation of a code compliant fire alarm and suppression system, and the repair of electrical conduit distribution throughout the facility. The project also repairs the exterior structural elements, replaces the failing standing seam metal roof, and corrects all life safety deficiencies while maintaining the elements of the building's exterior. The restored facility will meet minimum DOD Antiterrorism standards. All hazardous materials (HAZMAT) removed as part of the demolition will be disposed of following all state and federal guidelines. The Contract Duration is one thousand ninety-five (1,095) calendar days from Contract Notice to Proceed. TYPE OF CONTRACT AND NAICS: This RFP will be for one (1) Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract. The North American Industrial Classification System Code (NAICS) for this effort is 236220 - Commercial and Institutional Building Construction. TYPE OF SET-ASIDE: This acquisition will be a 100%Total Small Business Set-Aside. SELECTION PROCESS: This will be a two-phase Design/Build procurement process. The proposals will be evaluated using a Best Value Tradeoff source selection process. Potential offerors are invited to submit their performance, technical, and capability information as will be described in section 00 22 16 of the Solicitation, for review and consideration by the Government. The selection process for Phase I will evaluate such factors (not necessarily in order): Past Performance and Technical Approach for Design/Build. Pro Forma Information such as bonding and financial capability will also be required to meet the minimum requirements of the solicitation Following completion of the evaluation of Phase I, a target of five (5) of the most highly qualified offerors will be invited to participate in Phase II. The selected offerors for Phase II will be invited to submit additional information as will be described in Section 00 22 18 of the Solicitation, for review and evaluation by the Government. title: Multi-Ship Sustainment Partnership (MSSP) Single Award Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (SA-IDIQ) Contracts for Fleet Maintenance Availabilities and Incremental Selected Restricted Availabilities on DDG-51 Class Ships Homeported in Norfolk, VA
description: Portfolio Acquisition Executive Maritime (PAEM) is issuing solicitation N00024-26-R-4439 to procure a series of Multiple Ship Sustainment Partnership (MSSP) Single Award Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (SA-IDIQ) Contracts to complete Fleet Maintenance Availabilities and Incremental Selected Restricted Availabilities (ISRAs) on DDG-51 Class ships homeported in Norfolk, VA. Fixed Price with Award Fees (FPAF) Contracts will be awarded across Facilitized and Non-Facilitized Lots. Facilitized Lot includes Fleet Maintenance Availabilities and CNO scheduled ISRAs, to be completed on specific DDG-51 class ships that are scheduled to complete ISRAs over the MSSP period of performance. The scope of this lot includes all efforts necessary to support continuous coordination, planning and preparation between contractor and government to complete Fleet Maintenance Availabilities and ISRAs including, but not limited to, inter-availability preparation and administration (IAPA) support, inspections and assessments, engineering and design support, specification and other government furnished information reviews, and material procurement and logistics support. Unless otherwise specified in a Delivery Order Solicitation, all delivery orders for Fleet Maintenance Availabilities will be performed at the Government facility and all ISRAs will be performed in-plant at a Contactor-provided facility. The Navy will solicit this Lot on a full and open basis. The Navy intends to award up to three (3) Facilitized Lot contracts. The number will be determined at contract award based on the number of acceptable proposals received. Non-Facilitized Lot includes Fleet Maintenance Availabilities only, to be completed on specific DDG-51 class ships that are not scheduled to complete ISRAs over the MSSP period of performance. The scope of this lot includes all efforts necessary to support continuous coordination, planning and preparation between contractor and government to complete Fleet Maintenance Availabilities including, but not limited to, IAPA support, inspections and assessments, engineering and design support, specification and other government furnished information reviews, and material procurement and logistics support. Unless otherwise specified in a Delivery Order Solicitation, all Delivery Orders will be performed at the Governments facility. The Navy will solicit this Lot as a Small Business Set Aside. The Navy intends to award up to three (3) Non-Facilitized Lot contracts. The number will be determined at contract award based on the number of acceptable proposals received. Each contract will include three (3) one-year ordering periods. The supply being procured is the repaired, mission-ready vessel, which is returned to service within the Fleet. title: Advanced Technology Anti-Gravity Suit (ATAGS) Material Obsolescence/Prototype - RFQ
description: This Request for Quote (RFQ) is to establish a sole source contract for the Human Systems Division of the Air Force Life Cycle Management Center located at Robins Air Force Base, GA. This effort is for the procurement, construction and First Article Testing (FAT) of the Modified Advanced Technology Anti-Gravity Suit (ATAGS) which is a full coverage garment with bladders and Legacy G-Suits which is a cut-away trouser both are designed to counter G forces (or G-loc) experienced during maneuvers in high performance aircraft. AFLCMC\ROUS Body Wear IPT has identified obsolescence challenges associated with the Synergy Nomex material manufactured by Milliken and is currently used in the production of the modified ATAGS CSU-22/P and Legacy G-Suits CSU-13 B/P. To mitigate the obsolescence challenges associated with the Synergy material ROUS has discovered an alternative material that meets and/or exceeds the specification material requirements to produce ATAGS. Quantities projected and planned for this program are included in the Statement of Work (SOW), Contract Data Requirements List (CDRL), and other supporting documentation for this contract program. This effort will be executed as a Firm-Fixed Price (FFP) requirements contract consisting of a one (1) year basic period, Quantities are based on Best Estimated Quantities (BEQ). The solicitation will be issued in accordance with FAR 15, Contract by Negotiation. It is anticipated that FFP will be utilized for the majority of CLINs. The overarching contract will be issued to: Vinyl Technologies LLC. (Cage: 6T584) 200 Railroad Ave, Monrovia, CA 91016 Authority 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1) as implemented by RFO FAR 6.103-1, Only one responsible source, and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. Specifications, plans, or drawings relating to this procurement are not available and cannot be furnished by the Government as NO TECHNICIAL DATA is available and is proprietary to the identified source above. Foreign participation is prohibited. This requirement is not a set-aside. NO HARD COPIES WILL BE PROVIDED AND NO TELEPHONE REQUESTS WILL BE HONORED. Electronic procedures will be used for this solicitation. Responsible sources may identify their interest and capability and submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation which shall be considered by the agency. The Government does not own the data for these items. All questions and submissions to this requirement shall be submitted in writing to both of the following: Michael Carter: michael.carter.78@us.af.mil Audra Brown: audra.brown@us.af.mil All responses in reference to this synopsis shall be submitted no later than 21 December 2026, 3:00PM, EST. description: COMBINED SYNOPSIS/SOLICITATION NOTICE DESCRIPTION DETAILS The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Miami VA Healthcare System, Real Property Office, is performing market research with the intent of soliciting offers and awarding a lease with sufficient rentable square footage to yield 17,400 contiguous ABOA square feet of Medical Office and related space in Homestead, Florida. The space shall have a minimum of 150 parking spaces available. A lease up to 10 Years will be considered. New and Existing buildings will be considered. However, if not a newly constructed building, the space offered shall be in a Building that has undergone modernization, or adaptive reuse for the Space with modern conveniences and must be ready for occupancy no later than August 15, 2028. Space within or fronting on the following boundaries will be considered: North: SW 272 Street. South: SW 328 Street. East: SW 142 Avenue. West: SW 197 Avenue.. To be included in this procurement interested offerors responding to this RLP shall address ALL the following when responding to this advertisement: Cover Page contain the following information: Proposed property address with map showing property within the delineated area. Name, phone number and e-mail address of property owner. Available space. Number of parking spaces. Date space is available. Documentation evidencing that proposed property is outside the 100-year flood plain. Documentation supporting offerors ability to meet all the Government s requirements identified in this advertisement. Offers must fully comply with all requirements and supporting documentation mandatory as per the Terms and Conditions of RLP # 36C248-27-R-0012 and all exhibits attached to this announcement. All documents must be final, must be signed and must be acknowledged by placing the offeror's initials on each page. EXHIBIT M - RLP 36C248-27-R-0012 Deliverables Checklist has been included in this package to help Offerors determine the minimum documentation that needs to be included in the package. If claiming Socio-Economic status as Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) or Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB); offer must contain sufficient and clear documentation evidencing certified SDVOSB or VOSB status and must clearly show percentage of ownership and percentage of subcontracted work as well as the percentage of such work that will be done by SDVOSB or VOSB subcontractors. Any partnerships, joint ventures, or other type of associations; must clearly state and provide all documentation related to the percentage of participation of the SDVOSB or VOSB on all activities related to the lease during pre and post occupancy phases as well as percentage of ownership of the SDVOSB or VOSB firm in the partnership. If responding and you are not the property owner, i.e., broker, offer must include written signed statement from property owner (owner letterhead) authorizing you to represent the owner, in that case the offeror will be the owner, and all documentation provided must be signed by and completed accordingly. If not the owner but you responding with an offer on your behalf; the only acceptable document to demonstrate ownership/interest in the property is a notarized Purchase/Sale contract that has been signed by all parties, is not expired will remain in full force and effect and that is conditional only to the award (or not) of the lease resulting from this procurement. Any written agreement to acquire the interest may not include an option for the purchaser to assign its interest. Also, the offer must indicate that the offeror is willing to agree to include the following language in the Lease: within 30 days after execution of this Lease, Lessor will demonstrate it has obtained satisfactory title showing fee simple ownership of the property. Fee simple title must be free of any encumbrances that may limit the rights, responsibilities, or liabilities of the parties to this Lease. Lessor s failure to provide evidence of fee simple ownership within the specified timeframe shall give VA an immediate right to terminate the Lease for default. If a termination for default occurs due to the lessor s failure to provide fee simple ownership within the specific timeframe, the lessor will not be entitled to any payment whatsoever under the lease . A market survey of offered properties will be conducted by VA staff after offers have been received. Responses to this announcement are due no later than 3:00 PM ET on December 21, 2026, and must be submitted via email as follows: Department of Veterans Affairs. Office of Real Property. Attention: Javier Correa-Ochoa, Lease Contracting Officer. E-mail: javier.correaochoa@va.gov. THE GOVERNMENT IS LIMITED BY LAW (40 USC 278A, AS AMENDED 10-1-81) TO PAY NO MORE THAN THE APPRAISED FAIR RENTAL VALUE FOR SPACE. PLEASE NOTE: RESPONDENTS ARE ADVISED THAT THE VA ASSUMES NO RESPONSIBILITY TO AWARD A LEASE BASED UPON RESPONSES TO THIS ADVERTISEMENT

REQUIREMENTS The contractor shall maintain a quality control system which meets the requirements of Mil-I-45208A, Mil-Q 9858,ISO-9000 / 9001 / 9002 or equivalent. RESPONSIBILITY FOR INSPECTION: Unless otherwise specified, the contractor is responsible for the performance of all inspection requirements as specified herein. PROCEDURES:The contractor shall prepare and maintain Quality Control Documentation, test and repair procedures, and inspection procedures which shall be made available to the Government for review and approval. The procedures shall include sequential diagrams of the test, repair, and inspection process, as well as the performance spcifications to perform the procedures. QUALITY ASSURANCE PROGRAM PLAN: The contractor shall develop, implement and maintain a Repair Quality Plan in compliance with the requirements of Mil-I-45208A, Mil-Q-9858, ISO,9000 / 9001 / 9002, or equvalent.The plan shall define the specific methods by which compliance with contractual requirements will be assured. All quality assurance data shall be provided to the Government for review and approval upon request. PURCHASED MATERIAL CONTROL: The contractor shall establish and maintain a system of control over purchased material which shall assure that the necessary requirements of this contract are included. in all sub contract agreements. A parts control system shall establish a record of performance for each purchased and internally manufactured part and shall be used to evaluate continued use of the source. The contractors control system shall be in compliance wil either Mil-I 45208A/Mil-Q-9858 or equivalent Quality Quality Assurance Standared.(ISO/AS:9000, 9001, 9002). RECEIVING INSPECTION OF PURCHASED MATERIAL: Purchased items shall be inspected upon receipt at the contractors facility to assure conformance with all requirements of the Technical Data Package (TDP). Evidence of such inspections shall be maintained for Government review at least twelve (12) months following acceptance of the end item. Inspection reports shall be maintained by the contractor. The inspection report shall, at a minimum, include a record of all dimensional data (coordinate/positional), material, finish, and process with appropriate pass/fail criteria, such ascertifications, and actual dimensional readings. FAILURE ANALYSIS AND CORRECTIVE ACTION:All failure analysis and corrective action reports/plans shall be submitted to the Government. NONCONFORMING MATERIAL:The contractor shall establish an effective system for controlling nonconforming material including procedures for identification, segregation, and disposition. CONTRACTOR INTERNAL REVIEW BOARD (IRB):IRB authority is delegated to the contractor for this contract only. The IRB may be used only for disposition of materials exhibiting minor non-conformances, scrap or rework to return a part to conformance with drawings or specifications as authorized by the approved repair procedures.IRB shall not use "AS-IS" disposition. A complete file of IRB actions shall be maintained for review by the Government for concurrance of classification. MATERIAL REVIEW BOARD (MRB):Formal MRB authority for disposition of "AS-IS"and for minor non-conformances is retained by the Government. The contractor shall submit the appropriate request for Variance via the DCMC to the NAVSUP Contracting Officer. RESPONSIBILITY FOR COMPLIANCE: All items must meet all requirements of this Statement of Work. The inspection requirements set forth in this SOW shall become part of the contractors overall inspection system or quality program. The absence of any inspection requirements in the SOW shall not relieve the contractor of the responsibility of assuring that all Government equipment submitted for acceptance comply with all requirements. Sampling in quality conformance does not authorize submission of known defective items, either indicated or actual, nor does it commit the procuring activity to acceptance of any defective items. REPAIR ASSESSMENT TESTING: The Government may select samples of the Contract Line Items (CLINS) which have completed repair and have been accepted by the Government representative for the purpose of conducting performance testing, environmental testing, and quality conformance examination in a repair assessment test program. A quantity of CLIN's may be randomly selected from each quaterly repair production completion for shipment to the CFA or other Government designated location to conduct this testing. RECORDS OF DATA COLLECTION: The contractor shall maintain a historical record file to contain copies of applicable data and documents for individual CLIN's and assemblies by CLIN serial number. Mercury contamination of the material will be cause for rejection. If the inclusion of metallic mercury is required as a functional part of the material furnished under this contract, the Contractor shall obtain written approval from the Procurement Contracting Officer before proceeding with manufacture. The contractor's request shall explain in detail the requirements for mercury, identify specifically the parts to contain mercury, and explain the method of protection against mercury escape. Such a request will be forwarded directly to the Procurement Contracting Officer with a copy to the applicable Government Inspector. Upon approval by the Contracting Officer, the vendor will provide a "Warning Plate" stating that metallic mercury is a functional part of the item and will include name and location of that part. The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum).Sample the trapped air and if mercury vapor concentration is 0.01 mg/cu meter or more, the material is mercury contaminated insofar as the requirements of this contract are concerned. These requirements shall be included in any subcontract or purchase order hereunder and the Contractor shall insure SubContractor compliance with these requirements. Technical questions pertaining to these requirements shall be referred to the Procurement Contracting Officer via the cognizant Administrative Contracting Officer. For background, the following information is provided: Mercury is corrosive to gold, silver, nickel, stainless steels, aluminum and copper alloys. Stainless steels, nickel, and copper alloys are widely used in reactor plants and other submarine/surface ship systems. Accidental trapping of mercury in a component could cause serious damage to vital parts. Mercury is also toxic if inhaled, ingested, or absorbed through the skin. It is evident that grave consequences could result from small amounts of mercury vapor present in an unreplenished submarine/surface ship atmosphere. 3.6 ;Shipping / Storage notes from CG 81412 drawing#22-38894 apply: Note: Electrolysis module is filled with deionized water. -Do not allow the electrolysis module to freeze. -Do not leave the electrolysis module uncapped or unplugged. -Do not allow the electrolysis module internals to dry out. -The electrolysis module shall be flushed and filled with grade A quality water every 60 to 90 days.; 4. SCOPE 1.1 This contract/purchase order contains the requirements for manufacture and the contract quality requirements for the SERVER,AUTOMATIC DA . 2. APPLICABLE DOCUMENTS 2.1 Applicable Documents - The document(s) listed below form a part of this contract/purchase order including modifications or exclusions. 2.1.1 "Document References" listed below must be obtained by the Contractor. Ordering information is included as an attachment to this contract/purchase order. 3. REQUIREMENTS 3.1 Cage Code/Reference Number Items - The SERVER,AUTOMATIC DA furnished under this contract/purchase order shall be the design represented by Cage Code(s) reference number(s). Cage _______ ref. no. ;1LTM5 TI20-S86-1; 3.2 Marking - This item shall be physically identified in accordance with ;MIL-STD-130, REV N, 16 NOV 2012; . 3.3 Changes in Design, Material Servicing, or Part Number - Except for a Code 1 change, which shall be processed as provided in the code statement shown below, no substitution of items shall be made until the NAVICP-MECH Contracting Officer has notified and approval has been given by issuance of a written change order. When any change in design, material, servicing or part number is made to replace or substitute any item to be furnished on this contract/purchase order, the Contractor shall furnish, for the substituting/replacement item, a drawing and an explanation of the reason for the change, explaining the reason therefor. If finished detail drawings are not available, shop drawings in the form used by the manufacturer will be acceptable for Government evaluation. When notifying the Procurement Contracting Officer of the reasons for making substitutions, the type of change shall be indicated by code number in accordance with one of the following statements: Code 1: PART NUMBER CHANGE ONLY - If the Manufacturer's Part Number indicated thereon has changed, but the parts are identical in all respects, supply the item and advise NAVICP-MECH immediately of the new part number. Code 2: Assembly (or set or kit) not furnished - Used following detail parts. Code 3: Part not furnished separately - Use assembly. Code 4: Part redesigned - Old and new parts are completely interchangeable. Code 5: Part redesigned - New part replaces old. Old part cannot replace new. Code 6: Part redesigned - Parts not interchangeable. 3.4 Mercury Free - The material supplied under this contract/purchase order is intended for use on submarines/surface ships and therefore shall contain no metallic mercury and shall be free from mercury contamination. Mercury contamination of the material will be cause for rejection. If the inclusion of metallic mercury is required as a functional part of the material furnished under this contract, the Contractor shall obtain written approval from the Procurement Contracting Officer before proceeding with manufacture. The contractor's request shall explain in detail the requirements for mercury, identify specifically the parts to contain mercury, and explain the method of protection against mercury escape. Such a request will be forwarded directly to the Procurement Contracting Officer with a copy to the applicable Government Inspector. Upon approval by the Contracting Officer, the vendor will provide a "Warning Plate" stating that metallic mercury is a functional part of the item and will include name and location of that part. The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum).Sample the trapped air and if mercury vapor concentration is 0.01 mg/cu meter or more, the material is mercury contaminated insofar as the requirements of this contract are concerned. These requirements shall be included in any subcontract or purchase order hereunder and the Contractor shall insure SubContractor compliance with these requirements. Technical questions pertaining to these requirements shall be referred to the Procurement Contract
