title: M249 Squad Automatic Weapon (SAW), Ancillary Equipment, and Repair Parts in Support of Foreign Military Sales (FMS)
description: 1. Disclaimer and Important Notes This Sources Sought Notice is published solely for market research, planning, and information purposes in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 10. This notice does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quotation (RFQ), Invitation for Bids (IFB), or announcement of a forthcoming solicitation. The Government will not award a contract based solely on responses received under this notice. The Government will not pay for any information, materials, or documentation submitted in response to this notice, nor will it reimburse any costs incurred by respondents in the preparation of capability statements. Proprietary information, if submitted, must be clearly marked on every page containing proprietary data. The Government will handle proprietary information in accordance with applicable federal statutes and regulations. All material submitted in response to this RFI must be unclassified and properly marked. No manufacturer/distributor shall be given a copy of another manufacturer�s/distributor�s product information collected in this survey. Respondents are advised that telephonic inquiries or questions outside the designated point of contact email will not be honored. 2. Requirement Description & Scope The Department of the Army, Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) Maneuver Ground / Project Manager Soldier Lethality (PM SL), in conjunction with Army Contracting Command, is conducting market research to identify potential sources capable of manufacturing and delivering 5.56mm M249 Squad Automatic Weapon (SAW) systems, major subassemblies, spare parts, and associated logistics support to fulfill Foreign Military Sales (FMS) requirements. Scope of Supplies & Support: Weapon Systems: M249 Squad Automatic Weapon (NATO), including standard and short barrel variants, configured to standard U.S. Army / NATO operational standards. Major Components & Ancillaries: Spare barrel assemblies (standard and short barrel variants). 200-round ammunition feed containers/adapters. Collapsible and fixed buttstock assemblies, bipod assemblies, rail interface systems (MIL-STD-1913), and sling systems. Individual cleaning, maintenance, and tool kits. Spare and Repair Parts: Provisioning packages covering both depot-level and field-level repair parts, barrels, bolts, operating rods, receivers, trigger mechanisms, and springs. Logistics, Packaging, and Quality: Military packaging, preservation, packing, and marking (MIL-STD-2073 and MIL-STD-129). First Article Testing (FAT) / Lot Acceptance Testing (LAT) for proof, function, high-pressure resistance, and interchangeability. Preparation and compliance with foreign customs and International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) requirements. Training: Operator and Maintainer Training within and outside of the Continental United States. 3. Technical Data Package (TDP) & Licensing Considerations Interested parties must carefully note the following technical and licensing parameters: TDP Availability: The Government-held Technical Data Package (TDP) for the M249 platform is subject to restrictive rights and licensing provisions originating under Government Contract No. DAAA09-82-C-5361 with the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM), Fabrique Nationale Herstal (FN Herstal). Licensing and Export Rights: The governing license provisions contain specific terms governing foreign distribution, including an express Right of First Refusal reserved by the contractor for foreign military customer sales. Consequently, respondents must demonstrate that they either: Hold independent, unencumbered rights, proprietary tooling, and valid licenses to manufacture and export M249 weapon systems and parts for international third parties; or Maintain an existing valid commercial/licensing agreement with the OEM authorizing such production and distribution or are seeking to obtain a commercial/license agreement with the OEM. 4. Capability Statement Instructions Interested firms that possess the requisite manufacturing capabilities, facility clearances, and legal/licensing qualifications are invited to submit a Capabilities Statement Package. Submissions must not exceed ten (10) pages (excluding title page and executive summary) and should address the following areas: Part A. Corporate Background & Business Identification Company Information: Company Name, Address, and Website. CAGE Code and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) registered in SAM.gov. Point of Contact (Name, Title, Email Address, and Telephone Number). Business Socioeconomic Classification: Identify business size and status under NAICS 332994 (e.g., Large Business, Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Business, 8(a), HUBZone, Woman-Owned Small Business, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business). Facilities & Security: Manufacturing facility location(s) (must be compliant with applicable domestic sourcing and DFARS requirements). Current facility security clearance level (if applicable). Current Federal Firearms License (FFL) and Special Occupational Tax (SOT) status. Part B. Technical & Manufacturing Competence Manufacturing Experience: Summary of prior and current production experience with small-arms machine guns (specifically 5.56mm open-bolt, gas-operated systems) within the last five (5) years. Description of internal manufacturing capabilities (e.g., cold hammer forging, precision CNC machining, heat treating, phosphating/finishing, and automated assembly). Production Capacity & Throughput: Estimated monthly and annual production capacity for complete weapons and major spare components. Realistic lead times required from receipt of order to initial delivery. Quality Assurance & Testing: Overview of Quality Management System (QMS) certifications (e.g., ISO 9001:2015, AS9100). Description of on-site testing facilities capable of proof-firing, function verification, high-pressure endurance, and NATO interchangeability verification. Part C. Technical Data & Licensing Compliance Data Rights and Intellectual Property: Describe your access to, or ownership of, complete manufacturing drawings, material specifications, and tolerances required to build M249 weapons and parts without reliance on proprietary data belonging to third parties. Provide documentation or a detailed narrative explaining how your firm addresses third-party patent and licensing restrictions for foreign customer sales. 5. Submission Instructions Format: Only electronic responses are requested. Submissions must be in electronic format (Adobe Portable Document Format (.pdf) or Microsoft Word (.docx)), formatted for standard inch pages with 1-inch margins and a font size no smaller than 11-point (Times New Roman or Calibri). All material submitted in response to this RFI must be unclassified and properly marked. Delivery: Send submissions via email to the following points of contact: Contracting Officer: David DiRoma, Contracting Officer, ACC-DTA, Email: david.j.diroma.civ@army.mil Contract Specialist: Derek Ghilardi, Contract Specialist, ACC-DTA, Email: derek.j.ghilardi.civ@army.mil Subject Line Format: Response to Sources Sought - M249 FMS Requirement - [Company Name] Closing Date & Time: All responses must be received no later than 21 December 2026, 4:00 PM EST. Late submissions may not be considered in the Government�s market research synthesis. 6. Government Review and Follow-Up The Government reserves the right to review responses, contact respondents for clarifying discussions, and hold technical interchange sessions if deemed beneficial to the market research process. title: Brownsville Gateway U.S. Land Port of Entry Art in Architecture
description: The U.S. General Services Administration (GSA) Art in Architecture Program commissions American artists (Permanent Residents or Citizens of the United States of America ) to create publicly scaled and permanently installed artworks for Federal facilities nationwide. GSA is announcing an opportunity for a Federal art commission in conjunction with the new construction of the Brownsville Gateway U.S. Land Port of Entry in Brownsville, Texas. GSA is designing and constructing a new U.S. Land Port of Entry to replace the outdated Brownsville Gateway U.S. Land Port of Entry. The Land Port of Entry, once complete, will consist of multiple buildings for Federal inspection personnel who facilitate the transit of individuals and vehicles permitted entry into the United States from Mexico. GSA allocates one-half of one percent (0.5%) of the estimated construction costs of new or modernized Federal facilities for art commissions. The art budget for this project is estimated to be between $550,000 to $800,000. One or more artists will be awarded a fixed-price contract for a commission. Artists who wish to be considered for this GSA art commission must submit application materials to GSA by the SAM Contract Opportunity�s Response Date. Artists may also elect to be considered for all future GSA art commissions by submitting application materials to GSA�s National Artist Registry (Registry). Instructions on how to submit application materials and join the Registry are available on the following Web site: www.gsa.gov/real-estate/design-and-construction/art-in-architecturefine-arts/art-in-architecture-program/art-in-architecture-national-artist-registry All artists who wish to be considered as candidates for a commission at the U.S. Land Port of Entry in Brownsville, Texas, must have their application materials submitted and received by GSA by 5:00 PM Eastern Time, December 21, 2026. Artists� submissions received after the deadline will not be considered for this project but will be eligible for consideration on future GSA commissions alongside the other artists on the Registry. Artists already on the Registry need not resubmit but may elect to update their information prior to the deadline. GSA evaluates artists based on the following criteria: the media, materials, content and style of the artist�s past work, along with the artist�s past performance and experience with commissions or projects similar to the one described in this synopsis. Shortlisted artists will be contacted and asked to submit additional information, including a statement that the artist can perform the work associated with the GSA commission within the identified budget. GSA will count the combined weight of all the selection criteria as significantly more important than price. At minimum, the scope of services for this commission will require collaboration with the lead designer selected for the land port of entry project; travel to the project site; development and presentation of preliminary and final concepts; fabrication of the artwork; participation in meetings and conservation reviews as necessary; delivery and installation of the artwork; professional documentation of, and detailed maintenance planning for the artwork at the project site. For informational purposes: Artists selected for the contract award must be Permanent Residents or Citizens of the United States of America. Artists selected for the contract award will be required to have an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) at the time of award. However, SAM registration is not needed at the time of submission of application materials to GSA�s National Artist Registry. Instructions for creating an account and activating registration in SAM may be found at www.sam.gov. Artists selected for the contract award will be required to renew the registration in SAM on an annual basis for the duration of the project. In accordance with Executive Order 13934, Building and Rebuilding Monuments to American Heroes, GSA will prioritize the commission of works of art that portray historically significant Americans or events of American historical significance or illustrate the ideals upon which our Nation was founded.

title: Sanierung Haldenstrasse Einführung Trennsystem, Neubau Wasserleitung, Strasseninstandstellung
description:
Die Gemeinde Emmen beabsichtigt die Sanierung der Haldenstrasse mit Einführung des Trennsystems, Neubau der Wasserleitungen und Instandstellung des Strassenraums.

Die ausgeschriebenen Baumeister- und Belagsarbeiten umfassen insbesondere:

  • Neubau einer Mischwasserleitung (ca. 225 m, DN 500)
  • Neubau einer Regenabwasserleitung zum Augraben (ca. 86 m, DN 700–800)
  • Umnutzung der bestehenden Mischwasserleitung zur Regenabwasserleitung
  • Grabarbeiten für die Erneuerung der Wasserleitungen (DN 150 und DN 200)
  • Erstellung und Anpassung von Kabelrohranlagen und Fundamenten für die öffentliche Beleuchtung
  • Behindertengerechter Umbau der Bushaltestellen «Untere Wiese» und «Alp»
  • Anpassung der Strassenränder sowie Instandstellung der Strassen- und Trottoirbeläge

Die Bauarbeiten erfolgen etappenweise unter Aufrechterhaltung des Busverkehrs, des motorisierten Individualverkehrs sowie der Fussgängerzugänge.

Vorgesehene Bauzeit: April 2027 bis November 2028.

title: Rammeaftale for support og videreudvikling af Byggesag, Budget og Aftalesystem (BBA)
description: Bygningsstyrelsen ønsker at indgå en rammeaftale med én (1) leverandør til support og videreudvikling af fagsystemet Byggesag, Budget og Aftalesystem (herefter ”BBA”). Bygningsstyrelsen, som er ejendomsvirksomhed og bygherre for staten og universiteterne, kan gøre brug af rammeaftalen. BBA anvendes til økonomistyring af Bygningsstyrelsens bygge-, vedligeholdelses- og kunstprojekter. Systemet blev taget i brug i 2024 og er i stabil drift. Bygningsstyrelsen anser BBA for et forretningskritisk system. BBA er baseret på Navision Stat v.11.2 (ØSC Navision), som ejes og videreudvikles af Øko-nomistyrelsen på basis af Microsoft Dynamics NAV. I efteråret 2026 overgår BBA til Driftsmodel 1A (Applikationsdrift) i Statens IT, hvor Bygningsstyrelsen ejer og er ansvarlig for udvikling og ændringer af BBA, mens Statens IT har driftsansvar for BBA, middleware, operativsystem og underliggende driftsinfrastruktur. For at sikre relevans og anvendelighed vil der jævnligt være behov for videreudvikling og funktionelt vedligehold af BBA. En aktuel og kritisk udviklingsopgave vedrører Økonomistyrelsens opgradering af Navision Stat til Microsoft Business Central, som får afledte konsekvenser for BBA i 2027. Herudover er der i mindre omfang behov for ad hoc support til mindre vedligeholdelsesopgaver i den eksisterende konfiguration, herunder eksempelvis fejlrettelse vedrørende forbrugsopgørelser på enkelte byggesager. Der henvises til udbudsmaterialet. Udbudsbetingelserne indeholder en nærmere beskrivelse af opgaven og udbudsforløbet, og det øvrige materiale indeholder en beskrivelse af opgavens omfang.

title: NASA-WHITE SANDS SCRAP METAL REMOVAL TERM CONTRACT
description: This auction requires the high bidder to submit completed and signed certification(s) found in the "Documents" section and/or proof of licensing to the Sales Contracting Officer before the award is finalized. Requirements vary by auction. NASA-WHITE SANDS SCRAP METAL REMOVAL TERM CONTRACT GSA Auctions Link: https://www.gsaauctions.gov/auctions/preview/384008 IFB: 3-1-QSC-T-27-002 Location: National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) - White Sands Test Facility, 12600 NASA Road, MS RC, Las Cruces, NM 88012. The U.S. General Services Administration (GSA) is soliciting sealed bids for the purchase, onsite processing, and removal of Government-owned DEMIL A Mixed Metals Scrap at (NASA) - White Sands Test Facility. PROPERTY DESCRIPTION: Estimated Quantity: Approximately 129 gross tons (290,000 pounds) of DEMIL A Mixed Metals Scrap. Property may include heavy, structural steel, Oversize metal, steel assemblies and pipe. Moreover, metals may include flanges, metal tanks, machinery components, aluminum electrical wire with metals, mixed ferrous and non-Ferrous Scrap. The Contractor shall provide all labor, equipment, supplies, containers, transportation, and other resources necessary to support the Government�s scrap metal accumulation and removal requirements throughout the contract period. The Government will not furnish equipment, supplies, or labor for removal activities. The Contractor shall provide, service, replace, and remove containers, or perform direct scrap metal removal, as requested by the AGR and approved for use at the site. Requests may be made verbally, by telephone, or by email; however, email confirmation from the AGR shall serve as the official record for determining compliance with required response times. The Contractor shall maintain two 30-yard roll-off containers at the facility at all times for scrap metal accumulation. When a container becomes full, the Contractor shall remove and replace it with an empty 30-yard roll-off container within the required response time, unless otherwise coordinated and approved by the Government. The Contractor shall also be capable of supporting surge requirements associated with demolition projects or other increased scrap generation. During surge periods, the Contractor may be required to provide and service up to four additional 30-yard roll-off containers, in addition to the two 30-yard roll-off containers maintained at the facility. The Contractor shall meet the following response requirements: Container Delivery: Deliver requested containers within two business days after notification from the AGR. Container Removal/Replacement: Remove full or requested containers and replace them, as required, within two business days after notification from the AGR. Direct Removal: When container-based removal is not required, perform pickup, loading, transportation preparation, and removal within two business days after notification from the AGR, unless otherwise coordinated and approved by the Government. The Contractor must be capable of supporting routine, surge, and specialized removal requirements, including maintaining required containers, providing additional containers during surge periods, providing metal drums or other stationary containers as required, and providing crane support approximately one to two times within a 365-day period for removal of larger objects. Appendix C, Container Plan Submission Form (consolidated version), is required to be completed and included with the sealed bid documents. All removal activities shall be coordinated in advance with the AGR. Unless otherwise approved, removals should be scheduled for completion between 8:00 a.m. and 12:00 p.m. or between 1:00 p.m. and 3:00 p.m., excluding Fridays, Saturdays, Sundays, and holidays. Weighing will be performed using an on-site Government scale. Note: The attached removal history covers the last 24 months of the previous contract. The data was compiled from the monthly invoices and includes the removal frequency by month. All data regarding the weight is in gross tons. QUANTITY DISCLAIMER: The estimated quantity is provided for informational and bidding purposes only. The Government does not guarantee actual scrap quantity, weight, composition, value, or removal frequency. All property is sold strictly as scrap for recycling and recovery of material content. Resale, retention, or reuse of items or components as usable property is prohibited. CONTRACT TERM: The period of performance shall consist of a one (1) year base period, with up to two (2) one-year option periods, if exercised by the Government, for a maximum total contract term of three (3) years. BID PRICING: Billing totals are calculated as follows: Market Price: Monthly average of Fastmarkets MB-STE-0787 � Steel scrap shredder feed, fob Midwest, $/gross ton Apply Bid Percentage: Market Price � Bid Percentage = Adjusted Market Price Calculate Weight: Pounds, or Long tons calculated as Total Net Weight (lbs.) � 2,240 Billing Total: Adjusted Market Price � Calculated Weight Note: Bid abstracts from the two previous term contracts for the facility are attached for reference. The latest monthly averages from Fastmarkets, along with a sample invoice, have also been provided to help explain the monthly removal quantities/frequency, weights, pricing, and billing process. MANDATORY PRE-BID SITE INSPECTION: Attendance is REQUIRED for bid responsiveness. Bidders must coordinate inspections in advance with: Pedro "Pete" Rios, NASA - White Sands Test Facility Phone: 575-524-5138 (Office) / 575-779-6149 (Mobile) Email: pete.rios-1@nasa.gov Inspection attendance must be verified by the Government representative on Appendix A. IMPORTANT DATES (CENTRAL TIME): Questions Deadline: December 11, 2026 Sealed Bid Deadline: December 21, 2026, 5:00 PM CT Bid Opening: December 28, 2026, 9:00 AM CT SEALED BID SUBMISSION: Email the completed and signed Appendix A, Appendix C, and the Standard Form 114 (SF 114) as a PDF attachment to: westzonesealedbids@gsa.gov Subject: IFB 3-1-QSC-T-27-002 � Sealed Bid � Bidder Legal Name Appendix A, Appendix C, and the Standard Form 114 (SF 114) � Sale of Government Property are the only required sealed bid documents. SF 114C and Appendix B shall not be submitted with the bid. POST-BID / PRE-AWARD REQUIREMENTS: The Apparent High Bidder shall submit required documentation within 10 business days following written notification, unless otherwise directed by the Sales Contracting Officer. Requirements include Appendix B, insurance documentation, Contractor Capability and Responsibility Certification, and a $6,000 Performance Guarantee. The Performance Guarantee may be provided through cash Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) or an acceptable Irrevocable Standby Letter of Credit (LOC). An a Performance Guarantee are conditions of final award. IMPORTANT: Bidders must review the complete IFB, all applicable appendices, and solicitation documents before submitting a bid. Bids remain valid for 90 calendar days following bid opening. Award will be made to the highest responsive and responsible bidder in accordance with the IFB. This sale is subject to the IFB, GSAAuctions.gov Terms and Conditions, and SF 114C. In the event of an inconsistency, the IFB governs.

title: Denmark – Planting and maintenance services of green areas – Kontrakt om arealpleje til dansk politi og den centrale anklagemyndighed
description: Nærværende udbud omfatter kontrakt om arealpleje til dansk politi og den centrale anklagemyndighed (herefter benævnt Myndighederne). Kontrakten omfatter følgende serviceområder: 1) Grøn arealpleje og 2) Hvid arealpleje. Grøn arealpleje omhandler pleje og vedligehold af Myndighedernes grønne udendørsarealer inklusive faste og løse belægninger, særlige anlæg samt tagrender, bladfang og tag-brønde. Hvid arealpleje omfatter vintertjeneste på Myndighedernes udendørsarealer, herunder glatførebekæmpelse og snerydning af Myndighedernes parkeringsarealer, stier, trapper, ramper mv. Arealerne omfatter også arealer med offentlig adgang, herunder bl.a. fortov og gangarealer. Hvid arealpleje omfatter desuden en option, hvor Kunden har mulighed for at vælge mere miljøskånsomme glatførebekæmpelsesmidler. Udover ovennævnte serviceområder indeholder kontrakten bl.a. rapportering og vedligehold af data samt udarbejdelse af arealplejekort. Kontrakten forventes at omfatte ca. 171 lokaliteter af varierende størrelse med et nettoareal på ca. 500.000 m2 udendørsarealer fordelt over det meste af Danmark. Lokaliteterne består blandt andet af politistationer, administrationsbygninger og skoler. Der er for politiet ofte tale om samfundskritiske funktioner, der skal kunne fungere under særlige omstændigheder, herunder i tilfælde af særlige vejrforhold, katastrofer, opretholdelse af offentlig ro og orden osv. Af samme årsag er snerydning og glatførebekæmpelse særlig vigtig i forhold til sikring af fremkommelighed for politiets køretøjer og sikkerhed for medarbejderne ved snefald, frost osv. Derfor ønsker Myndighederne en leverandør, som understøtter dette behov og der er derfor knyttet særligt kritiske krav samt særlig KPI til disse ydelser. Myndighederne ønsker også, at leverandøren understøtter Myndighedernes fokus på bæredygtighed og grøn omstilling. Myndighederne ønsker at sikre en stærk systemunderstøttelse og en datadrevet tilgang til Kontrakten med betydeligt fokus på 1) brugervenlighed, 2) ensartet og konsistent dataindsamling og 3) direkte adgang til opgavedata. Myndighederne stiller bl.a. et FM-system til rådighed, som leverandøren kan tilgå via en leverandøradgang. Leverandøren har også mulighed for selv at etablere en automatiseret dataudveksling mellem leverandørens FM-system og Myndighedernes FM-system.

title: Z1DA--CON-NRM-663A4-24-209 Replace Fire Suppression Systems BLDG 61
description: Presolicitation Notice Presolicitation Notice Page 4 of 4 Presolicitation Notice *=Required Field Presolicitation Notice Page 1 of 4 663A4-24-209 Replace Fire Suppression Systems Building 61 VA Puget Sound Medical Center - American Lake 9600 Veterans Drive Southwest, Lakewood, WA, 98439 Procurement Number: 36C26027R0008 This is a pre-solicitation notice synopsizing an upcoming competitive solicitation for a planned construction requirement. An invitation for Request for Proposals (RFP) is anticipated to be posted on or about November 2, 2026. The Veterans Affairs (VA) Puget Sound Medical Center-American Lake located in Lakewood, WA, has a requirement for a Firmed Fixed Price construction project to Replace Fire Suppression System to Building 61. Description of Services: Project Number 663A4-24-209 Replace Fire Suppression System to Building 61. Contractor shall provide all labor, materials, and equipment to replace the fire suppression systems at Building 61 in accordance with the associated and published/provided contract 100% Construction Documents (Drawings, Specifications, etc.). The Government requires the newly replaced systems to operate seamlessly with the existing systems at the American Lake campus. The replacement of the existing systems is to be performed within tolerance delineated in the Manufacturer's Installation Instructions. The new replacement packages will be submitted in accordance with the contract submittal process and approved by the Government prior to the Contractor proceeding with any part of the scope of work. Work includes all associated aspects, including but not limited to, cutting and patching, and repair of finishes. Removal and disposal of existing equipment, materials etc. Replacement of the dry-pipe sprinkler system in the attic, including connection to existing fire alarm system and new nitrogen generator Installation of the new fire alarm control panel 1st, 2nd & 3rd floor replacement of sprinkler heads and installation of new fire alarm system Connection of the new fire alarm system to campus monitoring Removal of the existing fire alarm system Installation of new fire alarm control panel in building 62. The magnitude of this project is between $1,000,000.00 and $5,000,000.00. Period of Performance: The intended contract period of performance is 365 calendar days after receipt of notice to proceed. NAICS Code: The NAICS Code is 238210 "Electrical Contractors and Other Wiring Installation Contractors", with a size standard of $19M. The solicitation will be issued as a request for proposals (RFP) under FAR part 15 procedures and in accordance with the updated Revolutionary FAR Overhaul. A bid bond is required, and the bid guarantee amount shall be at least 20 percent of the bid price but shall not exceed $3 million. This project is 100% set-aside for Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses. All relevant solicitation documents, including specifications and drawings, may be accessed for download on the date of issue by conducting a search of Solicitation 36C26027R0008 on https://sam.gov/content/opportunities under Contract Opportunities. Any amendments to the presolicitation will be posted solely to this website. It is the responsibility of the offeror to verify the number of amendments issued. Prior to submitting an offer, (after solicitation is posted) all offerors must have an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM): https://www.sam.gov/SAM/ with a fully completed Representations and Certifications Section and SDVOSB firms must be certified by the Small Business Administration: https://www.sba.gov/, to be eligible for a federal government contract award. The Government is accepting industry comments. Comments may or may not be incorporated, at the discretion of the Government. The Department of Veterans Affairs Veterans Health Administration (VHA) Network Contracting Office 20 (NCO 20) anticipates making one (1) firm-fixed-price construction contract award based on a best value determination. An organized site visit is anticipated to be included in the details of the solicitation/RFP. All inquiries for this presolicitation shall be directed in writing to the NCO 20 Point of Contact- monique.king1@va.gov.
